summary: CRT file-descriptor handle release, structural twin of sub_595924. If descriptor index a1 is in range, the slot's flag byte at offset 4 has bit 0 set (slot in use), and the slot dword is not -1, optionally clears the console standard handle matching a1 when dword_5E65B4 == 1, resets the slot dword to -1 and returns 0; otherwise stores error 9 in the TLS error slot, clears the extended error slot and returns -1.

operations.description: Fail when a1 >= uNumber, or the flag byte at slot offset 4 (dword_8D4920[a1 >> 5] + 36 * (a1 & 0x1F) + 4) has bit 0 clear, or the slot dword is -1.

When dword_5E65B4 == 1, clear the console standard handle matching a1 with a null handle: a1 0 -> SetStdHandle(0xFFFFFFF6, 0), a1 1 -> SetStdHandle(0xFFFFFFF5, 0), a1 2 -> SetStdHandle(0xFFFFFFF4, 0).
Reset the descriptor slot dword at dword_8D4920[a1 >> 5] + 36 * (a1 & 0x1F) to -1.
Error path: write 9 through TLSOffsetGetter, write 0 through TLSOffsetGetter_afd8, and return -1.

unresolved: The descriptor table base dword_8D4920 (36-byte stride, indexed by fd >> 5 with element fd & 0x1F) is used by the raw source but is not present in the packet globals list; the 36-byte entry layout is inferred from the raw source.
The flag byte at slot offset 4 bit 0 is interpreted as an in-use marker only by symmetry with the assign twin; its independent meaning is unconfirmed.

The 0xFFFFFFF6/0xFFFFFFF5/0xFFFFFFF4 constants are the raw two's-complement renderings of the standard-handle ids; their meaning as STD_INPUT/OUTPUT/ERROR is derived from the SetStdHandle call pattern.
The caller HandleCloseWithErrorReporting (0x0058C38E) indicates this closes a handle on behalf of a close path, but the error-reporting linkage is not visible in this function body.
